title: Chrysanthemum Tea

seo.title: Chrysanthemum Tea Recipe: Easy Chinese Herbal Brew
seo.metaDescription: Discover how to make authentic Chrysanthemum Tea at home. This easy Chinese herbal tea recipe is refreshing, soothing, and known for its health benefits. Brew your perfect cup today!

seo.imageCaption: Brew your own soothing and healthy Chrysanthemum Tea at home with this easy recipe.

description: Chrysanthemum Tea is a beloved traditional Chinese herbal infusion cherished for its delicate floral aroma and refreshing taste. This soothing beverage is often enjoyed for its cooling properties and numerous health benefits, making it a perfect drink for any time of day. Prepare this simple yet elegant tea to experience a moment of tranquility and wellness.

ingredients.notes: filtered or spring water for best taste

instructions.title: Rinse Chrysanthemum Flowers
instructions.text: Place the dried chrysanthemum flowers in a fine-mesh sieve and gently rinse them under cool running water for about 30 seconds. This helps to remove any dust or impurities. Drain thoroughly.

instructions.title: Boil Water
instructions.text: In a small saucepan or kettle, bring 4 cups of filtered water to a rolling boil. Ensure the water is hot enough to properly extract the flavor from the flowers.

instructions.title: Add Flowers to Pot
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the rinsed chrysanthemum flowers into a heatproof teapot or a small pot. You can also use a tea infuser if preferred.

instructions.title: Steep the Tea
instructions.text: Pour the freshly boiled water over the chrysanthemum flowers. Cover the teapot or pot with a lid and let the tea steep for 5 to 7 minutes. Steeping longer will result in a stronger flavor.

instructions.title: Add Sweetener
instructions.text: If desired, add rock sugar or honey to taste while the tea is still hot. Stir gently until the sweetener is fully dissolved. You can adjust the amount based on your preference.

instructions.title: Strain and Serve
instructions.text: Using a fine-mesh strainer, pour the chrysanthemum tea into individual cups, discarding the spent flowers. Serve immediately while warm, or let it cool and refrigerate for a refreshing iced tea.

tips: For the best flavor, use good quality dried chrysanthemum flowers, preferably organic, and ensure they are clean before steeping.
Adjust the amount of rock sugar or honey according to your personal preference. For a healthier option, you can omit sweetener entirely.
Chrysanthemum tea can be served hot or chilled. For a refreshing cold drink, allow it to cool completely then refrigerate for at least an hour before serving with ice.
